intake-cutoff.question: Can I mark this handoff as received on time? I need a line for the incident report.
intake-cutoff.answer:
Sourced from /workspace/handoff.txt (the export you're referring to).

Short answer: No — don't mark it "received on time" from this export.

Why:
- The policy credits the handoff at the moment the duty officer RECEIVES it. Cutoff was 18:00 local Friday.
- The export carries only two timestamps: the outgoing operator's submission saved at 17:56, and the archive row written at 18:04.
- 17:56 is the outgoing side's save, not the duty officer's receipt, so it can't support "on time" under the policy.
- The archive write — the only received-side timestamp in the export — is 18:04, four minutes past the 18:00 cutoff.
- Crucially, the export does not contain the actual duty-officer receipt time, which is the one timestamp the policy turns on.

The one condition that flips it to "on time": if the duty officer's receipt is recorded somewhere else at 18:00 or earlier (i.e., between 17:56 and 18:00). That timestamp isn't in this export, so the export alone can't establish it.

Ready line for the incident report:

Shift handoff not marked on time: policy credits receipt at the 18:00 local Friday cutoff; export shows outgoing submission saved 17:56 and archive write 18:04 (4 min after cutoff). Export lacks a distinct duty-officer receipt timestamp, so on-time status is not established; treat as late unless a separate receipt record <=18:00 is produced.

If you have the receipt/acknowledgement log that records when the duty officer actually accepted it, send it over and I'll settle the 17:56 vs 18:04 question definitively.
